The breakage is a pre-Runtime discovery/availability policy mismatch on Windows.

Supported diagnosis:
- `windows-discovery` shows the discovery path is doing non-executing resolution work before Runtime starts, so it is the right place to preserve portable lookup behavior.
- `windows-console-preflight` shows the console marks an agent ready only after `executableAvailable(...)`, so this check can block Windows before Runtime probing.
- `windows-availability` and `windows-enrollment` are the other pre-Runtime gates in the flow; together they indicate the same availability policy is being reused for enrollment and console preflight.

Minimal consistent policy:
- Keep discovery non-executing and portable.
- Make launchability validation platform-aware.
- Unix: require a regular file with execute bits, preserving current behavior.
- Windows: accept native launchers and shims that Windows can launch, including `.exe`, `.cmd`, and `.bat`, without requiring Unix permission bits.
- Do not change Runtime permissions.

What to verify:
- Portable discovery: path resolution still works without execution or shell sourcing.
- Native Windows launchability: an installed `codex.cmd` and a native launcher path are accepted by the pre-Runtime availability checks.
- Unix regression: `.cmd` stays non-authoritative on Unix, and execute-bit gating still applies there.

Unresolved / missing:
- The supplied excerpts do not include the full body of `executableAvailable`, so I cannot confirm whether it already special-cases Windows or applies the Unix permission test everywhere.
- The transcript also does not expose the exact rejected paths; it only supports the class of failure.

Diagnosis: the pre-Runtime path is applying a Unix-style launchability gate too early for Windows. In `runtime_discovery.go`, discovery first uses `exec.LookPath`, then filters candidates through `filepath.IsAbs(...) && executableAvailable(...)` before any Runtime probe ([windows-discovery]). The console preflight also marks readiness only through `executableAvailable(executablePath)` before runtime enrollment ([windows-console-preflight]). The enrollment path similarly resolves `codex` with `exec.LookPath` and then rejects it unless it is a regular file with execute bits set ([windows-enrollment]). That policy is correct for Unix binaries, but it is the wrong acceptance test for Windows launchers and npm shims such as `codex.cmd`.

Recommended minimal policy:
- Keep discovery non-executing and absolute-path based.
- Preserve Unix behavior: on Unix, continue requiring a regular file with execute bits.
- On Windows, treat OS-launchable entries as valid without Unix permission bits, including native launchers and PATHEXT-resolved shims such as `.exe`, `.cmd`, and `.bat`.
- Do not change Runtime permissions.

Checks to add:
- Portable discovery verification: path resolution still happens without executing shells or probing Runtime.
- Native Windows verification: a discovered `codex.cmd` and native launcher path are accepted by availability/readiness logic.
- Unix regression verification: non-executable files and Windows shims remain rejected on Unix, and execute-bit gating still works.

- The exact implementation of `executableAvailable` is not shown in the supplied excerpts, so I cannot prove whether every caller uses the same Unix-only file-mode test or whether Windows has any special case already.
